analysis.answer: Current law allows parents of eligible public school children to receive 90 percent of state per-pupil funding in an education savings account for private educational expenses. This measure eliminates that program on July 1, 2028, and transfers any remaining account balances to the state school fund.

Families who rely on the program to pay for private tuition, tutoring, or online courses bear the cost of losing the state subsidy. The public school system benefits by retaining the per-pupil funding that would have gone to the accounts and by receiving any leftover balances.

Without the state subsidy, some families currently using the accounts to afford private schooling may re-enroll their children in public district schools, which would increase public school enrollment. Other families may choose to cover the costs of private options out of pocket.

The measure addresses the diversion of state education funds to private educational expenses. The mechanism is a complete repeal of the savings account program and a transfer of remaining balances to the state school fund.
This is a statutory change that can be amended or reversed by future legislation.

flags.note: Sets a specific future date for the program's repeal.
